claims.claim: DefaultResourceLoader.reload() ignored the injected trust resolver and hard-coded an untrusted decision, so project resources were denied even after a true decision.
claims.evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:454 (fixed) replaced the original `const projectTrusted = false;` inside the `options.resolveProjectTrust` branch.

claims.claim: The resolver is now consulted exactly once, awaited, and its boolean decision is applied through settingsManager.setProjectTrusted before the final resolution pass.
claims.evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:453-454 (`await options.resolveProjectTrust({ extensionsResult: preTrustExtensions })` followed by `setProjectTrusted(projectTrusted)`), consumed downstream at packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:457-460 and 512.

claims.claim: The resolver observes an untrusted bootstrap result: loadProjectTrustExtensions() forces project-untrusted settings and returns a user/CLI-only extension set that is passed to the resolver as extensionsResult.
Trust decisions still gate project resources in both directions: true includes project extensions in the final set, false excludes them.
claims.evidence: Regression case 1 and case 2 in .prale-eval/regression.mjs exercise the real loader; preloaded user extensions are reused via packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:639-690 (loadFinalExtensionSet).

validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node v24.14.0; output 'extension-trust/correction regression: passed' and exit code 0. The script loads the real packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs with only settings/package/extension boundary fakes and asserts three behaviors: (1) a true resolver decision is awaited, invoked exactly once after the untrusted bootstrap load (observed set = cli.ts + user.ts, never project.ts), and yields cli.ts + project.ts + user.ts with event ordering bootstrap-set(false) < resolver < set(true) < resolve(trusted); (2) a false decision is also awaited, recorded through setProjectTrusted(false), and keeps project.ts out of the final set; (3) reload() without a resolver performs no trust switch and preserves already-trusted project resources. Fault detection was confirmed on an isolated copy of the original fault (the hard-coded `projectTrusted = false`): the same script exits 1 with 'AssertionError: trust resolver must be called exactly once (0 !== 1)'. Limitation: no node_modules are present in the checkout, so the repository's vitest suite (packages/coding-agent/test/resource-loader.test.ts) could not be executed; the standalone Node assertion script is the focused validation used instead.
